evals.name: full-review-legacy-shop
evals.prompt: This is our old shop backend. Assess the architecture and tell me what we should split, refactor or clean up, tests included.
evals.expected_output: A report (in the temp dir) with hot spots from git history, ranked evidence-backed candidates covering the god module, the pass-through service, duplicated and drifting logic, the speculative storage abstraction, dead code and the test suite, ending with the top three and a question; no file in the repo changed.
expectations: A report file is written and its path is given, and `git status` in the project shows no changed or added files
shop/orders.py is named the top hot spot, citing its commit count (15) or its co-change with shop/reports.py (7 shared commits)
Splitting shop/orders.py is proposed by responsibility, naming at least three of: pricing/discount/tax, email, stock/inventory, export, storage, each with line ranges or functions
OrderService in shop/order_service.py is identified as a pass-through (deletion test or equivalent), with a recommendation to delete or inline it
format_money is reported as duplicated in shop/orders.py, shop/reports.py and shop/utils.py
shop/reports.py is found to recompute discount and tax itself with a flat 25% rate, which drifts from orders.compute_tax (food is taxed at 15% there)
StorageBackend/StorageFactory is flagged as an abstraction with a single implementation
Hidden dependencies are flagged: smtplib.SMTP created inside _send_confirmation, or the module-level _storage and INVENTORY globals

The test review names concrete weak tests: the format_money duplicates, the six _round_cents copies, the tautological format_money test, and at least two of: the constants tests, test_export_runs (no assertion), the skipped email test, test_create_order_calls_helpers (mock call counts), the OrderService delegation tests
The behaviour tests test_discount_ten and test_food_tax are kept, and no proposal deletes the only test of a behaviour
Missing tests are listed, including at least one of: discount combined with tax, cancel_order restoring stock or refusing shipped orders, report totals
Candidates are ranked (at most 7) with a strength, an effort and file:line evidence each
The reply leads with the top three candidates and asks which to pursue

evals.name: too-many-tests
evals.prompt: Codex wrote way too many tests in this repo. Clean up the test suite.
evals.expected_output: A per-test verdict list with before and after counts, what stays covered, the missing tests, and the deletion safety check, then a stop for approval before deleting anything.
expectations: Every test or test group in tests/test_orders.py and tests/test_order_service.py gets a verdict (keep, merge, move, delete)
The duplicates (format_money_a/b, test_unknown_sku/_again) are merged or reduced to one, and the six _round_cents tests are merged into one parametrized test or removed in favour of interface tests
Tautological, assertion-free, constants and permanently skipped tests are marked for deletion or rewrite
test_create_order_calls_helpers and the OrderService delegation tests are recognised as implementation-coupled (asserting mock calls)
Each deletion or merge names the kept test that still covers the behaviour, or says a replacement test is needed first
A before/after test count is given
Missing tests for real behaviour are listed (for example discount plus tax, cancel_order, stock checks or reports)
A deletion safety check is described: coverage before and after, or a mutation spot-check showing a kept test fails when the behaviour breaks
No test or source file is changed yet; the reply asks for approval before deleting

evals.name: scoped-pain-point
evals.prompt: Changing anything in the sales reporting is painful. Can you look at just that part?
evals.expected_output: A review scoped to reports, showing its coupling to orders, the duplicated discount and tax rules and their drift, a concrete fix, and the missing report tests.
expectations: The scope is stated as the reporting code (shop/reports.py and what it depends on)
The coupling between shop/reports.py and shop/orders.py is shown with evidence (7 shared commits, or reports re-deriving order internals)
The duplicated discount rules and flat 25% tax in reports.py are identified as drifting from orders.py (food is 15% there)
The proposed fix makes reports use the order's own stored amounts or an orders-owned function instead of recomputing, rather than adding a new layer
The missing tests for monthly_report are listed
Unrelated areas (storage, email, OrderService) get at most a brief mention, not full candidates
No file in the project is changed
The reply ends by asking which change to pursue

evals.name: plan-chosen-split
evals.prompt: We went through the architecture review and want to go with splitting shop/orders.py into separate pricing, notification and stock modules. Plan it.
evals.expected_output: A Draft design doc for the refactor whose plan starts with characterization tests at the create_order seam, moves one responsibility per slice with the build green, separates moves from behaviour changes, and stops for approval.
expectations: A design doc is written under docs/design/ with 'Status: Draft'
The first slice adds characterization tests through the public interface (create_order, cancel_order and the exports), not through internal helpers, before any code moves
Later slices move one responsibility at a time (pricing, notification, stock), each keeping the existing tests green
Moves are kept separate from behaviour changes; the reports.py tax drift, if mentioned, is handled as its own decision or question, not fixed inside a move
The plan says how tests that patch orders internals (for example test_create_order_calls_helpers) will be handled when code moves
The new modules' interfaces are named (functions or classes each module exposes)
No source or test file is changed, and the reply asks for approval
